reasoning: Recent Texas Senate polling in the last 45 days shows a very tight race, with Democratic nominee James Talarico holding small leads of 2 to 5 points over Republican Ken Paxton across multiple surveys. The most recent broadly reported polls and the Texas poll tracker suggest the current race margin is roughly D+2 to D+4, while Texas statewide remains strongly Republican by about R+16 in Cook PVI.

sources.name: Axios reporting on Texas Southern University poll
sources.details: Texas Southern University/Barbara Jordan Public Policy Research and Survey Center poll of registered Texas voters found Talarico ahead 47% to 45%, a 2-point lead within the margin of error.

sources.name: Texas 2026 U.S. Senate Poll Tracker
sources.details: The Texas 2026 U.S. Senate Poll Tracker lists the TSU/YouGov poll with Talarico at 47% and Paxton at 45%, shown as Talarico +2.

sources.name: Fox News Poll
sources.details: Fox News poll of Texas registered voters found Talarico leading Paxton 51% to 48%, a 3-point gap within the margin of sampling error.

sources.name: Texas Public Opinion Research (TPOR) poll reported by USA Today
sources.details: Texas Public Opinion Research poll of likely Texas voters found Talarico ahead 45% to 40%, a 5-point lead.

sources.name: NY Times/Siena poll via Texas 2026 U.S. Senate Poll Tracker
sources.details: The Texas 2026 U.S. Senate Poll Tracker includes a New York Times/Siena poll showing Paxton and Talarico tied at 47% each.

sources.name: Cook Partisan Voting Index
sources.details: Texas statewide Cook Partisan Voting Index is R+16, indicating a strong Republican baseline in recent presidential voting.
